_meta.how_to_regression_diff: Re-run (npm run check:golden whats-my-vibe) with dev backend up. Diff for QUALITY not exact match: HTTP 200, vibe_title/what_you_do/vibe_one_line present (guard keys). GUARDS: (1) no-inner-double-quote rule — the tool quotes the user's own writing; German/quoted phrases would 500 without single-quote substitution. (2) NO i18n-enum — SOURCE_TYPES are input pills, no AI-output enum is frontend-switched. NO format-strict fields. (3) guard keys top-level vibe_title, what_you_do (array + length), vibe_one_line. easy_to_misread can be JSON `null` by design (case 2 below) — the frontend's truthy check already hides it, this is NOT a bug. DO NOT reverse: the no-inner-quote rule; the guard on what_you_do being a non-empty array; the null-allowed contract on easy_to_misread.
_meta.known_issues: 2026-09-14 v2.1 round: v2 crossed from describing writing into inventing INTENT and specific reader thoughts — fixed with DESCRIBE EFFECT, NOT INTENT and READER IMPRESSIONS rules (see git history for detail). 2026-09-14 v2.2 round: v2.1 still (a) named specific hidden emotions the text never stated — called a 💀 emoji reaction 'this was mortifying' and a cancellation line 'self-aware embarrassment,' when the sample only supports comic framing of a mishap; (b) invented social purposes not demonstrated by the text — 'invites solidarity rather than judgment,' 'assumes the reader gets the vibe,' 'makes a reader feel included'; (c) enlarged easy_to_misread into a manufactured second reading ('gentle mockery of the feeling') when nothing in the sample supported real ambiguity. Added DO NOT NAME AN EMOTION UNLESS THE WRITING NAMES OR UNAMBIGUOUSLY EXPRESSES IT, DO NOT INVENT A SOCIAL PURPOSE, and KEEP INTERPRETATION CLOSE TO THE WORDS. Changed easy_to_misread from 'say honestly when none applies' (always a string) to null + omit when the wording doesn't support two genuinely plausible readings — same not-guard-required, null-allowed pattern as WhereDidTheTimeGo's try_this_next_time. Verified live on a case built from the exact reported sample (💀 dentist mishap, cancellation-plans PSA, ALL-CAPS oat-milk line): no named emotions, no invented social purpose, easy_to_misread correctly returned null. One soft residual: how_it_can_land still said the writer 'is inviting you to notice it too,' which echoes the banned 'invites solidarity' shape lightly — noted, not chased into a third round since every originally-reported phrase is gone.

input.samples: Per my earlier communication, I wanted to follow up on the outstanding deliverable we discussed. Moving forward, I think it would be beneficial to align on expectations to ensure we're all rowing in the same direction. Please advise at your earliest convenience.

output.vibe_summary: This sample is densely packed with formal business language and hedging phrases that create distance between the writer and the reader. Every sentence reaches for official-sounding terminology ('Per my earlier communication,' 'align on expectations,' 'rowing in the same direction') rather than stating something directly.
what_you_do: 'Per my earlier communication' opens by referencing a prior conversation without naming what was actually discussed, creating a sense of 'you should already know this' while remaining vague — the phrase has the effect of sounding formal and official while deflecting specificity.
The phrase 'outstanding deliverable' uses corporate jargon where 'thing you owe me' or 'project' might be clearer. This choice creates distance through abstraction and formality.

'I think it would be beneficial to align on expectations' uses softening language ('I think,' 'would be') combined with a business-speak verb ('align') instead of a direct request like 'let's agree on what's needed.' The softening has the effect of making a request feel more like a suggestion.

'Please advise at your earliest convenience' is a closing that invokes formality and politeness while making a demand — 'advise' is formal enough to feel slightly distant, and 'at your earliest convenience' adds a courteous buffer that can make an urgent request feel less pressuring on the surface.
The metaphor 'rowing in the same direction' introduces a casual phrase into otherwise stiff language, creating a jarring tonal shift — it stands out against the surrounding corporate vocabulary.
how_it_can_land: May come across as carefully professional and formal, with multiple layers of politeness buffering what sounds like it should be a straightforward ask.
Can read as indirect — the actual problem or request is wrapped in business terminology rather than stated plainly.
May feel cautious or hedged, with softening language ('I think,' 'would be beneficial') that keeps the writer at arm's length from making a direct request.
signature_moves: 'Per my earlier communication' — opening by referencing a prior exchange without restating it
'rowing in the same direction' — a sudden colloquial metaphor interrupting formal language
'Please advise at your earliest convenience' — politeness and urgency wrapped together in formal phrasing
Stacked jargon phrases ('align on expectations,' 'outstanding deliverable') rather than plain language
output.easy_to_misread: The opening 'Per my earlier communication' assumes the recipient remembers what was discussed without restating it. If the earlier conversation was vague, forgotten, or involved multiple people, this reference could land as passive-aggressive or make the reader unsure exactly what deliverable is being referenced. The writer may intend simple reference-building; a reader may interpret it as a subtle reproach for not following up sooner.
output.vibe_one_line: Formal and hedged — every direct thought gets wrapped in business jargon and politeness, with a casual metaphor breaking through the surface.

cases.name: casual social posts, no genuine ambiguity (EN) — easy_to_misread is null by design

input.samples:
just a girl who forgot she had a dentist appointment and found out the hard way 💀

living for this random Tuesday sunset though, no context needed

reminder that you're allowed to cancel plans and it doesn't make you a bad person, it makes you tired

okay but why did nobody tell me oat milk in coffee changes EVERYTHING

output.vibe_summary: This writing treats small life mishaps and observations as shareable moments, using exaggeration and deadpan framing to turn the mundane into something wry and relatable. The voice feels conversational and self-aware without apology.
what_you_do: Opens with physical comedy and emoji reaction ('forgot she had a dentist appointment and found out the hard way 💀') — the skull emoji stands in for a nonverbal reaction, creating a sense that the writer is laughing at themselves rather than dwelling on inconvenience.

Juxtaposes trivial and meaningful in the same sentence ('living for this random Tuesday sunset though, no context needed') — treats a sunset with the same energy as a major life event, which flattens the hierarchy and makes both feel equally worth noticing.

Delivers soft advice as a casual PSA ('reminder that you're allowed to cancel plans...') — the framing as a 'reminder' to others creates distance from the statement while still asserting it, so the writer positions themselves as peer-observer rather than authority.

Uses ALL CAPS for emphasis on a small discovery ('oat milk in coffee changes EVERYTHING') — escalates the intensity of language for something objectively minor, creating a humorous mismatch between the language scale and the actual stakes.
how_it_can_land: Can read as playful and self-aware — the writer notices their own absurdity and is inviting you to notice it too.
May come across as warm and unguarded — treats readers as people who also forget appointments and get excited about coffee.
Can feel conversational rather than performed — short, punchy sentences with natural rhythm, as if speaking aloud to friends.
signature_moves: Exaggeration paired with emoji: 'found out the hard way 💀'
Absurd intensity for small moments: 'oat milk in coffee changes EVERYTHING'
Topic-hopping without transition (dentist → sunset → life advice → coffee discovery)
Self-aware framing: 'just a girl who forgot...', 'reminder that you're allowed...'
output.vibe_one_line: Unfiltered, funny-because-it's-true observations delivered with exaggerated stakes and zero pretense.
